When you enter the final leg of the game, your sidekick leaves you. So you get a few blissful hours of not having to hear him yammer on. Then the final boss beats your ass, but it skips to a cutscene of your old side kick, travelling the countryside. And he's still yammering on, but now you've had time to miss it. He letting everyone you've helped over the course of 50 hours know that now you need their help. So everybody prays for you, and sends you their good vibes, and you recover and can now beat the boss.

I came home that night, after a ridiculously long day - and bought flower immediately. Launched it, and I have never felt a connection like that with another video game before.

No timer, no.. instructions. Just mechanics, and a story told without words.

That first level... the beautiful rolling green hills, the surround sound grass whipping past.

Call me a flamer, if you must, but I don't think anything will get past that feeling I had the night I played flower for the first time.

Also I played flower on mushrooms a few weeks later - I would heavily suggest this to anyone with a heart.

It's been pointed out that recreating this sub in the image of /r/WATMM may not be the best idea, and, while I only partially agree, I do think that this is a rare opportunity to provide new solutions and a new sense of community surrounding the music makers of voat.

Here are some thoughts:

  • Weekly feedback threads. These, in my opinion, were a positive staple that the old WATMM offered. It's been noted that WATMM was too broad, and I can empathize with that; as a futurebeat producer, I had a hard time giving feedback to garage rock bands that posted. So here's a potential solution: weekly feedback threads where each day covers a different, broad genre (i.e., metal Monday's, alt rock Tuesday's, edm Wednesday's, etc.) with each of these threads starting off with the rules and links to relevant subverses. I these are just examples, but hopefully we can flesh it out with time.

  • Collaboration between various subverses. I know other music creation subs already exist, and others will be created. If each has its own voice, this sub could be a hub to welcome newcomers and point them in the right direction towards their interests.

  • To self-promote, or not to self-promote? For now, this sub is small and can afford self-posts to user-created music. On reddit, however, there was an explicit separation between works in progress (WATMM) and completed (listen to this). While this may not be an issue we have to address now, we will eventually have to address it and we may wish to do so differently from reddit.

What do you think? And if you guys have other potential issues you've noticed (as well as potential solutions for solving them), let them be known!

Edit1: It seems that /v/listentothis is closer to /v/music, and /v/showoffyourmusic is for user-created content. Also, /v/musicproduction is for just that, production (e.g., edm, futurebeat, experimental electronica, mastering tracks), so this sub could still be specific to music creation as a whole.

Edit2: Some more specific subverses that could be added to the sidebar include:

  • /v/showoffyourmusic

  • /v/musicproduction

  • /v/makinghiphop

  • /v/trapproduction

  • /v/edmproduction

  • /v/futurebeatproduction

If you find more, let me know!
